Five days stale and 100% wrong, while carrying its own how_to_refresh command that nobody ran. That is MA59/MA60 one level up: a hand-typed snapshot of something git already knows.
_meta.why_not_a_generated_file_in_its_place: MB27 proposed committing a GENERATED board plus a test that fails when it is older than the newest branch tip it describes. Measured, that assertion cries wolf: the board's own strongest ingredient - worktrees carrying uncommitted work, 8 of 12 on the day this was written - changes whenever anybody saves a file, so a committed snapshot goes stale within minutes and the pin would be red on ordinary work. MA21's failure mode reached by a pin instead of by a warning. A generated snapshot rots exactly like a hand-typed one; it just rots honestly. So there is ONE copy of the fact and it is git. `board_state.py --write` emits a snapshot on request, to a gitignored path, for handing to another session.
_meta.what_it_could_never_see: Its own caveat named the hole: an agent editing files in a worktree with nothing committed yet was invisible to it. board_state.py measures that directly, and it read 8 of 12 worktrees dirty on the day the hand file was retired.
